title: Take It Apart, Build It Again

scenes.visual: Title card 'Take It Apart, Build It Again' over a turkey sandwich on whole-wheat bread. COLOUR MAP (both films): simple sugar = GOLD hexagon block; amino acid = BLUE round bead; nucleotide = GREEN bead with a small phosphate tab; fatty acid = ORANGE wavy tail; glycerol = ORANGE comb with three teeth; water = small LIGHT-BLUE bent 'V' labelled 'H2O'; links = short GREY bars between blocks. Two counters sit top right whenever links form or break: 'links' and 'waters'. All blocks are labelled cartoons, not molecular structures; every number appears only as on-screen text.

scenes.tts: You eat a turkey sandwich, and some of it goes on to become part of you. How can a wheat plant and a bird turn into part of a person?
scenes.visual: Sandwich at left, a cartoon teenager outline at right; a dotted arrow from sandwich to body with a large question mark on it. Small wheat stalk and bird icons pop up above the bread and the turkey.
scenes.narration: You eat a turkey sandwich, and some of it goes on to become part of you. How can a wheat plant and a bird turn into part of a person?

scenes.tts: Zoom into the bread. Its starch is a long chain of small sugar blocks. Now zoom into the turkey. Its proteins are chains of a different kind of block, amino acids of many kinds.
scenes.visual: Camera pushes into the bread slice: a chain of GOLD hexagons joined by GREY bars, label 'starch'. Camera slides to the turkey: a chain of BLUE beads, each bead carrying a different small letter, label 'protein: amino acids of many kinds'. Both chains wiggle gently.
scenes.narration: Zoom into the bread. Its starch is a long chain of small sugar blocks. Now zoom into the turkey. Its proteins are chains of a different kind of block, amino acids of many kinds.

scenes.tts: Each small block is called a monomer. A long chain of them is a polymer. Think of beads on a necklace, though real chains fold and coil.
scenes.visual: One GOLD hexagon pops out, label 'monomer'. The whole chain glows, label 'polymer'. A bead necklace briefly overlays the chain, then the chain bends and coils away from the straight necklace; small tag 'the analogy breaks: chains fold'.
scenes.narration: Each small block is called a monomer. A long chain of them is a polymer. Think of beads on a necklace, though real chains fold and coil.

scenes.tts: In your gut, the chains come apart. A water molecule slips into one link, and the link breaks. Splitting with water is called hydrolysis. One water, one broken link.
scenes.visual: The GOLD starch chain floats in a pink gut tube. A LIGHT-BLUE 'H2O' V drifts to one GREY bar; the bar snaps and one GOLD block drifts free. Counters: links 5 to 4, waters used 0 to 1. Label 'hydrolysis = splitting with water'.
scenes.narration: In your gut, the chains come apart. A water molecule slips into one link, and the link breaks. Splitting with water is called hydrolysis. One water, one broken link.

scenes.tts: Here is a chain of six sugar blocks. How many water molecules will it take to break every link?
scenes.visual: A fresh chain of six GOLD hexagons, numbered 1 to 6 on screen. A question card: 'Waters needed?' Counters read links ?, waters ?.
scenes.narration: Here is a chain of six sugar blocks. How many water molecules will it take to break every link?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question card holds; a 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: Five. Six blocks have only five links between them. Each water breaks one link. So it is one water per link, not one per block.
scenes.visual: Five LIGHT-BLUE V's arrive one by one, each snapping one GREY bar. Counters tick: links 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0; waters used 1 to 5. On-screen text '6 blocks, 5 links, 5 waters'. The six GOLD blocks drift apart.
scenes.narration: Five. Six blocks have only five links between them. Each water breaks one link. So it is one water per link, not one per block.

scenes.tts: The freed blocks leave the gut and reach your body's cells. There, the job turns around. Instead of taking chains apart, the cell builds new ones.
scenes.visual: Loose GOLD hexagons and BLUE beads stream along a red blood-vessel tube into a round cartoon cell outlined in grey, label 'body cell'.
scenes.narration: The freed blocks leave the gut and reach your body's cells. There, the job turns around. Instead of taking chains apart, the cell builds new ones.

scenes.tts: Inside the cell, the blocks join into new chains. Compare the free blocks with the finished chain. One water's worth of atoms is missing at each link. Building by removing water is called dehydration synthesis.
scenes.visual: Inside the cell, two BLUE beads click together with a GREY bar; a dashed LIGHT-BLUE 'H2O' V appears in a tally box at the side, labelled 'water missing, counted from free blocks'. Repeat three times. Counters run the other way: links 0 to 3, waters 0 to 3. Label 'dehydration synthesis = making by removing water'.
scenes.narration: Inside the cell, the blocks join into new chains. Compare the free blocks with the finished chain. One water's worth of atoms is missing at each link. Building by removing water is called dehydration synthesis.

scenes.tts: Now count it the other way. Breaking a chain of six blocks took five waters. A chain of six built from free blocks is five waters short. One per link, either way.
scenes.visual: The six GOLD blocks from the reveal slide back together in reverse; at each new GREY bar a dashed LIGHT-BLUE V drops into the tally box. Counters run up: links 0 to 5, waters 0 to 5. On-screen text 'build 6 blocks: 5 links, 5 waters'.
scenes.narration: Now count it the other way. Breaking a chain of six blocks took five waters. A chain of six built from free blocks is five waters short. One per link, either way.

scenes.tts: Joining blocks does not happen for free. Joining takes energy. In cells, each kind of molecule is built by its own energy-using route. So the real steps usually release other products, not water. The water count is bookkeeping for the atoms. Taking apart adds water. A built chain is one water short per link.
scenes.visual: Each of the four block types arrives beside its own small, unnamed energy-source icon (a different icon for each type), with the on-screen label 'a different route for each kind of molecule'; at the join a small grey shape labelled 'other product' leaves instead of a V, while the tally box still adds one dashed V. Caption 'real steps differ; the atom count holds'. A circular arrow appears: 'take apart (add water)' on top, 'build (one water short per link)' on the bottom.
scenes.narration: Joining blocks does not happen for free. Joining takes energy. In cells, each kind of molecule is built by its own energy-using route. So the real steps usually release other products, not water. The water count is bookkeeping for the atoms. Taking apart adds water. A built chain is one water short per link.

scenes.tts: Look at the new protein. Its amino acids sit in a different order from the turkey's. A turkey protein does not become your protein. Its blocks are reused.
scenes.visual: Two BLUE bead chains side by side, each bead carrying a small letter: top row labelled 'turkey protein', bottom row labelled 'your new protein', with the same beads in a shuffled order. Arrows trace three beads from top row to new positions in the bottom row.
scenes.narration: Look at the new protein. Its amino acids sit in a different order from the turkey's. A turkey protein does not become your protein. Its blocks are reused.

scenes.tts: Cells use four kinds of block: simple sugars, amino acids, nucleotides, and the fatty acids and glycerol of fats. They build four classes of large molecule. The text sorts out which block builds which.
scenes.visual: The four block types slide in side by side: GOLD hexagon 'simple sugar', BLUE bead 'amino acid', GREEN bead with tab 'nucleotide', ORANGE comb with three ORANGE tails 'fatty acids + glycerol'. Under them four empty labelled boxes appear: 'carbohydrates', 'proteins', 'nucleic acids', 'lipids'.
scenes.narration: Cells use four kinds of block: simple sugars, amino acids, nucleotides, and the fatty acids and glycerol of fats. They build four classes of large molecule. The text sorts out which block builds which.

scenes.tts: So the sandwich does become you, block by block. Digestion adds one water for each link it breaks. Counted from its free blocks, each new chain is one water short per link.
scenes.visual: Replay in fast motion: the starch chain breaks as LIGHT-BLUE V's go in, blocks travel to the cell, and new chains form while dashed V's drop into the tally box ('counted from free blocks'); no water floats out of the cell. Both counters show equal numbers at the end.
scenes.narration: So the sandwich does become you, block by block. Digestion adds one water for each link it breaks. Counted from its free blocks, each new chain is one water short per link.

scenes.visual: End card with the Hex mascot. Take-home line: 'Each link: one water added to break, one water short when built.'
